title: Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman finds no halakhic ruling stated in his name; he appears in the patronymic chain in [Berakhot 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26a.15): “Rav Mari son of Rav Huna son of Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba said”; there at [31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.31a.13) it reads “Mari, grandson of Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba”; Hyman proposes reading “son of Rav Huna.” Hyman suggests that possibly what they said in [Pesachim 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.43a.2) — “Rav Huna bar Yirmeyah said: What is oil of myrrh? Stacte; and Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba said,” etc. — is Rav Huna his son, mentioned before his father because the Gemara afterward brings a proof for Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba from a baraita; therefore his father is mentioned last. Some wish to say that Rav Huna without further designation was the son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba; Hyman rejects this, as explained in his entry.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Berakhot 26a gives Rabbi Yirmeyah and continues the chain with Rabbi Yochanan. Berakhot 31a calls Mari a grandson of Rav Huna. Hyman proposes “son” and tentatively connects Rav Huna with the name in Pesachim.
